subject: Safety Net proposal and audit trail — close timeline risk
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@helixhealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Safety Net proposal and audit trail — close timeline risk

Lisa,

Thanks again for the candid update on the evaluation window. We heard the procurement constraints and the internal product gating — understood. Given the slippage risk, Camila and I sketched a lightweight "Safety Net" proposal to reduce final-mile exposure without changing the core SOW. High level:

- Short-term: a two-week acceptance-window buffer (soft-lock) + priority support during cutover.
- Financial: limited credit holdback tied to acceptance milestones (not to exceed 5% of monthly committed units).
- Governance: a one-page MAP amendment + an audit trail log for all milestone sign-offs.

I've attached a quick spreadsheet with the proposed milestones and triggers (safety-net-summary.xlsx). If Helix can commit to the amended MAP sign-off cadence we can preserve the current go-live quarter while giving your procurement team time to finish the paperwork.

Can you confirm whether procurement can sign a MAP amendment (not a full reprocurement) and whether the credit-holdback construct is acceptable? If so, we'll circulate a one-page amendment and a DocuSign link.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Sr. Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0183

Attachment: safety-net-summary.xlsx (spreadsheet — milestones & triggers)
From: Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@helixhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Safety Net proposal and audit trail — close timeline risk

Marissa — appreciate the quick follow-up.

Short answer: procurement prefers not to reopen the main SOW, but a narrow MAP amendment sounds workable as long as legal signs off. Two practical constraints from my side:

1) Our legal requires explicit acceptance gates and an audit trail of sign-offs; a one-page amendment is more likely to get fast approval.
2) Finance needs clarity on how the credit holdback gets reconciled if acceptance is delayed more than 30 days.

I'm copying procurement so they can confirm timelines. If you can send a draft MAP amendment with clear acceptance language and the reconciliation table, I can fast-track it through legal.

—Lisa
Lisa Tran
Director of Product — HelixHealth

Subject: Draft: Safety Net MAP amendment (proposal)

Lisa / team —

Based on Marissa's note and your constraints, attached is a lean draft amendment that preserves the existing SOW but layers in the Safety Net mechanics. Key items included (summary):

- Acceptance gates: 3 discrete sign-off events (Integrations smoke test, Pilot acceptance, Final acceptance). Each sign-off requires a named approver and timestamped sign-off to feed the audit trail.
- Buffer: a 14-calendar-day buffer added to the final acceptance window (soft-lock) that triggers priority support and mitigation tasks.
- Credit holdback: up to 5% monthly credit applied only if final acceptance is delayed beyond the buffer for reasons outside Redwood's documented remediation scope.
- Reconciliation: finance reconciliation table that shows how holdbacks get credited back in the following billing cycle if acceptance completes within 30 days.

Attachments:
- MAP_Amendment_v2.pdf (draft amendment)
- safety-net-summary.xlsx (milestones & reconciliation table)

Ask: Please confirm whether Helix legal can accept a short-form amendment and whether procurement needs additional language around escrow or SLAs. If acceptable, Marissa and I will prepare a DocuSign envelope and a HubSpot note referencing HLX-9421.

Camila Reyes
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft: Safety Net MAP amendment (proposal)

Lisa — thanks for the quick clarity. Two follow-ups from my side as we're prepping the MAP amendment to be exec-ready:

1) Audit trail format — can Helix accept a simple signed PDF with embedded timestamps and the HubSpot activity feed as the canonical log? That keeps us out of heavyweight tooling.
2) Escalation ladder — given this close-date drift, we want to formalize an exec-level notification if the buffer is breached. Proposed ladder:
   - T+0: technical remediation (PM/Eng)
   - T+3 business days: Camila + Helix technical lead sync
   - T+7 business days: Sales leadership (Marissa / Helix Dir. Product)
   - T+14 business days: Exec sponsor notification and optional credit trigger review

If procurement/legal need alternate language, flag required redlines by end of day Wednesday (9/2). We'll keep the amendment intentionally short — one page + reconciliation table — so procurement can route quickly.

Jonas Weber
VP, Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Per the thread above, attached is the amended one-page MAP + reconciliation appendix (MAP_Amendment_v2.pdf). Quick summary of next steps so everyone has the cadence:

1) Helix legal/procurement to provide any redlines by EOD 2026-09-02.
2) If no redlines, Redwood will send DocuSign envelope by 09/03 with the two named approvers for Helix (Product and Procurement).
3) Once both approvers sign, Redwood will enable the 14-day buffer and set the MAP audit-trail doc in HubSpot (link included).
4) If buffer is breached for reasons outside Redwood's remediation, the finance reconciliation table governs the credit holdback.

Please acknowledge receipt and confirm the Helix approvers (name + title + email) we should populate in the DocuSign envelope.
